parsed.notes: Lens A refutes only the Plain View Doctrine Key home-role assertion; the case identity and core good-faith holding are supported by the disclosed lake record and cached opinion text.

reasons: The lake identity record names United States v. Ganias, court 2d Cir. en banc, decided 2016-05-27, year 2016, docket 12-240-cr.
The lake citation fields match the asserted official citation, parallel citation, and vendor-neutral citations.
The opinion states that Ganias appealed tax-evasion convictions and that the court affirmed because reliance on the 2006 warrant was objectively reasonable good faith.
The opinion expressly leaves the Fourth Amendment retention question undecided while describing retention of non-responsive mirrored data from the 2003 search and the later 2006 warrant.
The opinion records that the prior panel found a Fourth Amendment violation and ordered suppression, while the en banc court affirmed instead on good-faith grounds.
residual_risks: Lake pinpoints are empty, so support depends on the cached opinion text rather than curated pinpoint records.

defect.evidence_quote: we need not decide whether a Fourth Amendment violation occurred
defect.locator_note: home: Plain View Doctrine; role: Key
defect.problem: The case is not supported as a Key Plain View Doctrine authority from the disclosed opinion or lake record. The opinion is about digital mirror retention, particularity/general-warrant concerns, and Leon good faith; it does not analyze or apply the plain-view doctrine.
defect.proposed_fix: Remove the Key home role for Plain View Doctrine, or downgrade it to a non-key related link only if the destination page expressly uses Ganias for digital over-retention context. A better home would be good-faith exception, exclusionary rule, digital over-seizure/over-retention, or particularity.

reasons: A full-text search of the disclosed opinion shows no plain-view doctrine discussion.
The page's own holding and rule frame the case as a Leon good-faith disposition leaving the retention question open, not as a plain-view holding.
residual_risks: The undisclosed Plain View Doctrine page might discuss adjacent anti-exploratory-search themes, but that would not make this case a Key plain-view authority on the disclosed record.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Use Ganias as an unresolved digital retention/good-faith case, not as a key plain-view case.

reasons: Treatment fields in the content page match the lake treatment object: unverified validity, null as-of fields, unverified composite basis, false varies_by_point, and the same frontier-stub scope note.
residual_risks: Subsequent treatment and currency are outside lens A and were not substantively reviewed.

reasons: The disclosed lake identity verifies this as a Second Circuit en banc court-of-appeals case, matching the in-circuit Second Circuit weight label as framed.
No contrary treatment or limiting authority appears in the disclosed lake treatment fields, which are unverified rather than adverse.
residual_risks: Authority weight and currency are primarily lens B territory; lens A did not perform a substantive treatment review.
